clue.text: Predict yacht can become a form of psychotherapy

indicators.note: the clue says the answer plus the word yacht can be rearranged into another form, so these letters are reshuffled together

explanation.surface: A prophet claims a boat might somehow turn into a kind of talking therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer's letters plus YACHT, shuffled by 'can become a form of', make PSYCHOTHERAPY. Take YACHT away from that word's letters and arrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To foretell what will happen is to make a prophecy; the verb form spelt with an S means predict.

clue.text: Champion among nationalists turned nuts

indicators.note: turned means the combined letters are read in the opposite direction
among means one set of letters sits within the other

parts.note: SNP is the Scottish National Party, the main Scottish nationalists
an ace is a champion or expert

explanation.surface: A winner surrounded by nationalists went crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like an adjective for the mad nationalists, but it is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Pecans are a kind of nut from a North American hickory tree, so the plural fits nuts.

clue.text: Dense fog — Central tube station first to get disrupted

indicators.note: central picks the middle letter of the word fog
disrupted means the letters are thrown out of order
first picks the opening letter of the word station

explanation.surface: Thick fog at a Central line Tube station causes the first disruption of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central' takes the middle of fog, O; 'disrupted' rearranges TUBE plus S into BTUSE. Central is also a London Underground line, which helps the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Dense in the sense of slow-witted or stupid is a synonym for this word, which describes someone slow to understand.

clue.text: Delighted with the Guardian's stated time for an economy round

parts.note: delighted means happy

indicators.note: stated signals that the next word is said aloud and spelt as a word that sounds the same

parts.note: the Guardian refers to itself as we, so the Guardian's is our

explanation.surface: The Guardian, pleased, announces a time slot.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appears in the Guardian, so 'the Guardian's' is OUR; spoken, OUR is indistinguishable from HOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub's cheap-drinks period lets you buy a round of drinks at lower prices, an economical round.

clue.text: Only one to escape being stamped on?

definitions.text: Only one to escape being stamped on?

parts.words: Only one to escape being stamped on?
parts.note: the sole of a shoe takes every step, so in a pun it is the thing that keeps surviving being stamped on; the plain sense is the last one left alive

explanation.walkthrough: The plain sense is the only person to come through a disaster; the question mark points to the sole of a boot, which survives being stamped on.
explanation.definitionFit: The last person left alive after a disaster is the lone one who escaped death.

clue.text: Cordial hospital not in the frame

indicators.note: not in means the letter is left out of the frame word

parts.note: a chassis is the frame of a car
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A hospital offers a soothing drink but leaves it out of the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Crème de cassis is a blackcurrant liqueur; a cordial is a sweet fruit drink or liqueur.

clue.text: Stalag ground is filled with hostility

indicators.note: the words Stalag ground are filled with the answer, which runs across them unbroken

explanation.surface: The grounds of a prisoner-of-war camp are full of ill feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: A Stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British slang for aggressive trouble or hostile behaviour, short for aggravation.

clue.text: Aware of extremely subversive and evil intent

indicators.note: extremely picks the extreme letters, first and last, of subversive
evil suggests corruption, so the letters of intent are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone conscious of a deeply subversive and wicked plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentient being is one able to perceive and feel, conscious of its surroundings.

clue.text: Trivial as whitebait?

parts.note: unimportant people are called this, and whitebait are literally tiny young fish

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means people of no importance; taken literally it describes whitebait, the tiny young of herring and sprat.
explanation.definitionFit: Insignificant people or things are known by this phrase, and baby fish are fry, so whitebait are literally little ones.

clue.text: Weapon religious group deployed round a water source

indicators.note: the group's letters are spread out around the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a cult is a religious group, often a fringe one
a tap is where water comes from

explanation.surface: A sect sends out a weapon around a spring.
explanation.definitionFit: A catapult is a device for hurling stones, an old siege engine or a child's slingshot.

clue.text: Items finish in oven

indicators.note: in places the word for finish within the word for oven

parts.note: an Aga is a British brand of range cooker, a heavy kitchen oven
the end is the finish

explanation.surface: Things come to an end inside a cooker.
explanation.walkthrough: An AGA is a heavy cast-iron range cooker common in British country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: A meeting's list of things to discuss consists of numbered items of business.

clue.text: Indigenous person, putting head down among tribe, starts to show superb ingenuity

indicators.note: among puts one set of letters inside the tribe's name

parts.note: the Cree are a First Nations people of Canada

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, is moved down to the bottom of the word

parts.note: a native is an Indigenous person

indicators.note: starts to picks the first letters of show and superb

explanation.surface: An Indigenous person, bowing among the tribe, begins showing great inventiveness.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cree are a First Nations people of Canada; 'putting head down' sends the first letter to the bottom of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Inventiveness and originality, the quality of making new things, is a close synonym for ingenuity.

clue.text: Curious opposites are back-to-back

indicators.note: back-to-back puts the two opposite words with their backs touching, so one of them faces the other way

parts.note: the opposites are yes and no; written one after the other with no turned round they read Y-E-S-O-N

explanation.surface: Something odd: opposites are placed rear to rear.
explanation.walkthrough: Put NO and YES with their backs touching: NO, then YES facing the other way, SEY. Written as a single string reversed, YESON gives the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Inquisitive or prying, as in sticking one's nose into others' business, is what curious means here.

clue.text: As tailor, may be? That's about right

definitions.text: As tailor, may be? That's about right

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the other letter
may be hints that the letters could be something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark about tailoring: being like a tailor is about right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges AS TAILOR to SATORIAL, and 'about' wraps that round R. The whole clue also describes the answer, so it is an all-in-one.
explanation.definitionFit: Sartorial means relating to tailoring or the way someone dresses.

clue.text: 'Latch heartless Doctor Faust', wrote von Goethe, bitter at the end

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letters, the heart, are removed from Doctor and from Faust
at the end picks the last letter of each of wrote, von, Goethe and bitter

explanation.surface: A quotation from Goethe's Faust, bitterly describing the doctor as a fastening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes CT from DOCTOR and U from FAUST, leaving DOOR and FAST; 'at the end' gives E, N, E, R. Goethe wrote Faust, about a scholar called Doctor Faust.
explanation.definitionFit: A latch is a simple catch that keeps a door shut, a fastening device for it.

clue.text: Firmness and kindness to start hand in glove after outbreak

indicators.note: after places the glove part after the broken-out letters

parts.note: split as out and break, the word asks for the letters of out broken up and rearranged

indicators.note: in places one letter within the glove word
start picks the first letter of hand

explanation.surface: Firm but kind treatment, at first hand-in-glove, after a disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outbreak' is read as out broken, an anagram of OUT, giving TOU; H from 'to start hand' goes 'in' GLOVE to make GHLOVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being strict with someone for their own good combines firmness with care for them.

clue.text: We are its reincarnation, so to speak

indicators.note: a reincarnation is the same thing reborn in a new form, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Speaking figuratively, we are its rebirth.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are idioms that flag a figurative or loosely chosen expression, as one might say.

clue.text: Stop, but not to see the woman's frolics in water

indicators.note: but not means the following word is taken out of Stop

parts.note: lo is an old word for see, as in lo and behold
the woman is she, and the woman's, short for the woman is, is she's

explanation.surface: Stop, but the woman's still playing about in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' removes TO from STOP to leave SP.
explanation.definitionFit: To move about noisily in water, splashing and playing, is what this verb means.

clue.text: Haughty Louis IV moving forward — chasing fancy cup, sire?

indicators.note: chasing means the Louis part comes after the other part
fancy suggests something elaborate and imaginative, so the letters are rearranged
IV is four in Roman numerals, so the fourth letter of the name moves one place forward

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A French king is moving forward after chasing a fancy cup, your majesty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges CUP SIRE to SUPERCI; Louis's fourth letter, I, moves up one place to make LIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Supercilious describes someone who behaves as if superior to others, disdainful and arrogant.

clue.text: Internet mob broken up

indicators.note: broken up means the letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: An online mob is broken up.
explanation.walkthrough: Split Internet into INTER, which is the definition, and NET, which with MOB is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to bury a body, and to entomb is to place it in a tomb.

clue.text: Solvent sexy male, fine bottom half

indicators.note: the bottom half picks the second half of each of the words sexy, male and fine

explanation.surface: A dating ad: a sexy man with a fine backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Xylene is an aromatic hydrocarbon used as a solvent in paints and laboratories.

clue.text: Tasty offshoot in book

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the book word

parts.note: a tome is a large book
split as off and shoot, the word asks for the letters of shoot knocked off into a new order

explanation.surface: A tasty side branch tucked into a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offshoot' is read as shoot thrown off, an anagram of SHOOT making OOTHS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something toothsome is good to eat, delicious, so tasty is a synonym.

clue.text: Treacherous, unlike Jacob

definitions.meaning: dangerous or risky, as in a hair-raising situation
in Genesis Jacob was a smooth man while his brother Esau was covered in hair

explanation.definitionFit: Informally, a scary dangerous situation is described this way, and Esau's body, unlike his twin's, was covered in hair.

clue.text: Hungary's borders accessible

parts.note: the borders of the word Hungary are its outer letters, the first letter H and the last letter Y

explanation.surface: Hungary's frontiers are easy to get to.
explanation.walkthrough: The outer letters of HUNGARY are H and Y, and that phrase, written as one word, is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something conveniently close at hand and easy to reach or use is accessible.

clue.text: Cultural Revolution's end, in principle

indicators.note: in places the last letter inside the word for principle

parts.note: an ethic is a moral principle

indicators.note: end picks the last letter of Revolution

explanation.surface: The Cultural Revolution's end, in principle.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes China's Cultural Revolution, but 'Cultural' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethnic means relating to a group sharing a culture, traditions and origin.

clue.text: Disappear, having heard comic 'encore'

indicators.note: having heard signals that the comic's title is spoken and spelt as words that sound the same

parts.note: The Beano is a long-running British children's comic
an encore is a call for more

explanation.surface: Someone vanishes after a comedian is called back for an encore.
explanation.walkthrough: THE BEANO is a British children's comic paper; said aloud it gives BE NO.
explanation.definitionFit: To cease to exist, to vanish for good, is a way of saying disappear.

clue.text: Tries to be outrageously sassy after early start

indicators.note: after puts the shuffled letters following the single letter
start picks the first letter of early
outrageously suggests wild behaviour, so the letters of sassy are thrown about

explanation.surface: Someone attempts outrageous cheek right from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: To essay something is to attempt it, so essays as a verb means tries.

clue.text: Come together with capacity to contain revolutionary chaos

indicators.note: to contain means the capacity word holds the other letters inside

parts.note: being able means having the capacity to do something

indicators.note: revolutionary means the word turns round, read backwards

parts.note: a mess is chaos

explanation.surface: People gather, able to hold back revolutionary chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: To assemble is to gather in one place, meeting as a group.
